surfaces.part: top header cap of the sign board
green panel face with white Korean lettering

answer.evidence: Rows 1-3 are a light band (L about 238) at the top. Row 4 is a mid-gray front-edge line (L=132, #738a90). Row 5 is a dark row that works as eave shadow. Together these give a top band of about 4 rows with a front-edge line and shadow. The green face runs from rows 6 to 29 (24 rows) and carries the white lettering, with a slightly darker divider at rows 18 and 29. Row 30 is a lighter base line and row 31 is the outline. The narrower widths in rows 0-2 (10, 12, 14) are rounded corners, not an ellipse. No side face is drawn. The top band is thin but meets the edge-line-plus-shadow criterion, so I read it as a three-quarter view with a small top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical dark-green sign board with a light border, white hangul text and a short base. Its measured facts sit within the shipped modern_city range: 9 visible tones per tile against 6 (bus-shelter-a), 12 (kiosk-a) and 20 (vending-a). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so the board is not a flat fill; the lettering and border break up the panel. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans green and dark teal, matching the material rather than a black sticker line. It has about 4 shading steps (border highlight, panel mid, panel dark, deep edge), a little below the 5-6 on the richer references. It is still above bus-shelter-a, which is accepted art, and it is a simple, thin signage prop. Seen next to the references at the same scale, it looks equal in crispness and not noticeably flatter than bus-shelter-a, though it has less surface grain than vending-a.
